entry.title: Merge Holiday Album to Feature Original New Poronographers, Tubs Songs
entry.summary: One of them is called “I Am an Elf”
entry.content:
It’s getting dark before 5 p.m. again; luckily, there’s a new Merge Records holiday compilation to help keep the gloom at bay. Out digitally this Friday, November 13, Snowed In promises such delights as a brand-new Tubs song called “I Am an Elf” and Charlotte Cornfield’s take on “Jingle Bells.” Scroll down for the full track list.

Snowed In is the sequel to Merge’s 2019 holiday album, You Wish. Other chestnuts this go-round include Dawn Richard’s “On a Night Like This,” Fruit Bats’ “O! Holy Night,” and label newbie Elanor Moss doing Judee Sill’s “Jesus Was a Cross Maker.” The New Pornographers and Superchunk also recorded original songs, “Some Wings” and “Shortest Day of the Year,” the latter of which you can hear below.

entry.title: Jeanne River Recruits Cameron Winter for Debut Single
entry.summary: “PP2” introduces the Brooklyn singer and electroacoustic composer, with prepared piano from the Geese frontman
entry.content:
Jeanne River, the leftfield folk project of Brooklynite Jeanne Hill, has debuted with a Cameron Winter-assisted single called “PP2.” The Geese prodigy plays prepared piano on the bric-a-brac tune; Hill contributes vocals, ukulele, celesta, production, and other technical duties that make use, in part, of an Ampex MM1200 reel-to-reel tape machine. Hill also made the cover art with photographer Liselotte Davis, which you can find below, along with the video.

Budding Jeanne River fans can catch her tomorrow (November 12) at Night Club 101 in Manhattan, on a bill with Caroline’s Jasper Llewellyn. A Philadelphia show supporting Joanne Robertson is lined up for April 8, 2027.

entry.title: Beyoncé Recreates Sade’s Love Deluxe Album Cover
entry.summary: She also paid homage to Diana Ross in a new i-D feature
entry.content:
Beyoncé might not say much of anything outside her music but she’ll never pass on an opportunity to gush about Sade, from shouting her out in a Harper’s Bazaar interview to posting a handwritten letter on her website about what the singer means to her. “For years, I've turned to Sade for inspiration,” she wrote in 2012. “I cannot even begin to count the nights, days, hard times—when I need her—she is there, to inspire me, and brighten me. Her music has been a true friend, as all true music should be.”

Bey’s latest Sade tribute? Recreating the 1992 Love Deluxe cover, in a new photo shoot and (likely emailed) interview in i-D Magazine. Alas, the Beyoncé Q&A doesn’t mention Sade herself—it’s largely about the hair product line Cécred—but it does include another homage, to Diana Ross’ Forever boxset art. You can check that one out over on i-D. Sade is set to be inducted into—but not appear at—the Rock Hall on November 14.

entry.title: Phoebe Bridgers, Slayyyter, Billy Strings to Headline Hinterland 2027
entry.summary: The three-day music festival returns to St. Charles, Iowa next summer
entry.content:
Hinterland Music Festival is headed back to Iowa next summer for another long weekend of middle-American field frolicking. Pitchfork can exclusively reveal the 2027 lineup, which features headliners Phoebe Bridgers, Slayyyter, and Billy Strings, plus a wider bill including Caroline Polachek, Underscores, Remi Wolf, Westside Cowboy, Horsegiirl, Tiffany Day, and more. Check out the full slate below. Hinterland 2027 takes place from July 30 to August 1.

Since its first edition in 2015, Hinterland has been held in St. Charles, which sits a roughly 30-minute drive south of Des Moines. The 2026 lineup boasted Oklou, Ninajirachi, Lorde, Jane Remover, Geese, and Kali Uchis, among others.

All three of Hinterland’s headliners next year will be performing on the heels of hot-ticket tours. Bridgers wraps up the European leg of her dates in support of Lost Weekend this December, and Billy Strings just extended a 2027 run behind the T Bone Burnett-produced So Much for Goodbyes through next June. Slayyyter, who concluded her Wor$t Girl in the World trek last month, will precede her Hinterland show with a Madison Square Garden headlining debut.

entry.title: Oklou Scored a New Animated Film
entry.summary: The first song off the In Waves soundtrack, “The Swirl Ahead," is out now
entry.content:
Oklou has penned the score for a new animated feature, In Waves, set to land on Netflix next month. She collaborated with the French artist ROB on the 23-song soundtrack, which is out alongside the film on December 11. You can check out a first preview, “The Swirl Ahead,” below.

Directed by Phuong Mai Nguyen, In Waves is adapted from AJ Dungo’s 2019 graphic memoir of the same name, which charts the romance between a young surfer and skateboarder as they pursue their passions and navigate personal struggles. It premiered earlier this year at Cannes Film Festival, becoming the first animated film selected to open Cannes’ Critics Week.

The release caps off a big year for Oklou, who just closed out the second run of an extensive tour in support of her 2025 album Choke Enough. The trek included her Coachella debut back in April, plus headlining dates at Primavera Sound, Lollapalooza, and All Points East. Last year, she also released a deluxe edition of the album that featured a song with FKA twigs, “Viscus.”

entry.title: Matthew Dear Gets “Dizzy” on New Song
entry.summary: The producer’s comeback continues after a pair of summer singles
entry.content:
Matthew Dear has kept a relatively low profile since his 2018 album Bunny. That has begun to change: This summer, the techno producer released “New Drug” and “Head in the Clouds” for the French label Salon, his first tracks since the 2022 single “Talking Sleep.” Now, he is back at his alma mater label Ghostly with a formal comeback single. Listen to “Dizzy” below.

Of the song’s nocturnal soul, Dear writes in a press release:

There is a time of night, somewhere between midnight and dawn, when most people are asleep. That’s when I've made some of my favorite music. ‘Dizzy’ was born in that space. A space that lets me operate differently, from somewhere that feels dreamlike. For me, writing songs has to be a little out-of-body. I have to find a personality trait, or some part of my subconscious, and let that version of myself take the wheel for a while. When everyone else is asleep, it's easier to do that.

‘Dizzy’ is a love song from the middle of the night, set on a dark two-lane highway, told from the perspective of someone caught in the cycle of coming and going from the person they love. The smell of asphalt cooling under the moonlight hangs in otherwise empty air. It’s neither humid nor dry, hot nor cold, living nor dead.

Dizzy. In love.

Dear wrote, produced, and performed the single, before Scott Lake picked up the mix and master at Subterranean Sound Studios. Since releasing Bunny, Dear has released an EP under the alias Brain and retrieved his lost album Preacher’s Sigh & Potion for a 2021 release, having shelved it in 2008.

entry.title: Naima Bock Signs to Fire Talk, Celebrates With a Horse in New Video
entry.summary: A European tour is also on the books for spring 2027
entry.content:
Naima Bock has signed to Fire Talk and released a new song, “Rocks,” which you can listen to below. Formerly of Goat Girl and, as a solo artist, Sub Pop, the London-based singer-songwriter has also signed with Bristol indie Breakfast in the United Kingdom. Her new single comes with a pleasant video co-starring a horse. Check it out below, along with Bock’s upcoming European tour dates.

Since 2024’s Below a Massive Dark Land, Bock has released a standalone single, “Rolling,” and toured with Dinosaur Jr. and Jake Xerxes Fussell. She said in a press release that the “Rocks” “came to me on a rainy autumn night as my flight was ascending to somewhere less cold. I’d been listening to Palace Music non-stop for a month. Writing it saved me from my chronic oscillation between to-be home and not-to-be home, that is when I decided I would do both.”

Revisit Andy Cush’s review of Naima Bock’s 2022 debut album, Giant Palm.

entry.title: Watch Tinashe Bring Popstar to The Tonight Show
entry.summary: She performed the title track and “Melatonin,” and paid brief homage to Janet Jackson
entry.content:
Tinashe’s acclaimed Popstar run continued apace on Wednesday, as she dropped by The Tonight Show Starring Jimmy Fallon to perform a double dose off the new record: a brief orchestral take on its title track along with dance-pop single “Melatonin.” She also appeared to throw in a brief homage to Janet Jackson’s 1994 Saturday Night Live performance of “Throb.” (In 2024, Tinashe spoke to People about her love of Janet: “She is my biggest idol, my biggest reference. I’m constantly referring to her. The best album of all time, to me, The Velvet Rope is top-tier.”)

Tinashe is set to bring Popstar on the road next spring, with her The Show Must Go On tour, which kicks off in April. A full run of dates can be found here.

entry.title: Armand Hammer Surprise-Release New Album, Snakes & Ladders
entry.summary: Elucid and billy woods’ new project features $ilkmoney, Kenny Segal, and Clipping.
entry.content:
Armand Hammer have surprise released their latest album, Snakes & Ladders. The duo of Elucid and billy woods dropped the LP overnight, via Backwoodz. Check it out below.

The follow-up to their 2025 project with the Alchemist, Mercy, Snakes & Ladders features production from Clipping., Saint Abdullah & Eomac, Kenny Segal, and Preservation, among others. DJ Haram and $ilkmoney drop in for guest vocals.

The duo is currently closing out a North American tour, playing in Seattle tonight and Denver Friday before ending the run at Brooklyn’s Music Hall of Williamsburg on Sunday.

Read more about Armand Hammer in Pitchfork’s The 100 Best Rap Albums of All Time.

entry.title: Coachella 2027 Lineup: Tame Impala, SZA, and Dua Lipa
entry.summary: Madonna and Phoebe Bridgers are also on the bill, with Daddy Yankee in the fourth headliner spot
entry.content:
Following weeks of speculation and some SZA-related leaks, the Coachella 2027 lineup is finally, officially here. The S.O.S. singer is set to headline, as she more or less confirmed already, alongside Tame Impala and Dua Lipa. Other performers include Madonna, Phoebe Bridgers, Weezer, Don Toliver, and, as the fourth-billed headliner, Daddy Yankee. The festival returns to the Indio desert from April 9 to 11 and 16 to 18.

Other highlights include the return of Caroline Polachek; high-profile pop and R&B bookings including Robyn, Zara Larsson, Steve Lacy, Kelela, and Kehlani; rising stars and alternative darlings like Drain Gang, Underscores, Bassvictim, Muna, Shygirl, Magdalena Bay, and Snow Strippers; and a spread of dance titans ranging from Four Tet, Underworld, and Giorgio Moroder to Tiësto and Peggy Gou. Angine de Poitrine, Social Distortion, and Pinegrove join the rock ticket, and the rest of the bill is a typically eclectic mix of critics’ darlings (Xaviersobased, Nirosta Steel, the Avalanches, Zack Fox) and the likes of Adéla and Måneskin. Also featured: the debut of a Justice show called Blinded by the Lights.

Both Kevin Parker and SZA know their way around the main stage, the former having headlined in 2019—becoming the first Australian artist to do so—and the latter having joined Justin Bieber as a surprise guest at this year’s festival. Dua Lipa made a surprise appearance of her own, in 2017 with Martin Garrix (also returning this time around), but, like SZA, this is her first time headlining the festival in her own right. Madonna’s return to the desert, for the second year running, is set for the Dance Tent, the site of her 2006 Confessions on a Dance Floor show.

Sabrina Carpenter, Justin Bieber, and Karol G were last year’s headliners. Carpenter recruited a host of special guests for her two sets: Susan Sarandon and Sam Elliott for Weekend One, and Madonna for Weekend Two. (Madge left the desert a few items of clothing shorter than she arrived.) Dijon, Slayyyter, Oklou, and Geese—who covered Bieber’s “Baby”—all played their first full sets at the festival. Read more about everything that went down in The Best and Worst of Coachella 2026.

Passes for 2027 go on sale this Friday at noon Pacific, with an AmEx presale starting 24 hours earlier. The festival will once again stream on YouTube.

entry.title: King Gizzard & the Lizard Wizard Announce New Album Entropy, Two North American Tours
entry.summary: It’s a companion LP to their last album, Alien Metal
entry.content:
King Gizzard & The Lizard Wizard are releasing a new album, Entropy, on December 4, a companion to the Eurorack explorations of previous LP, Alien Metal. The rock band have also announced two North American tours taking place next year, one in August and the other October. Below, check out the full tour slate and the project’s first single, “Rogue Wave.”

The band originally planned to release Entropy and Alien Metal at the same time, however, after hitting challenges recording Alien Metal, “Entropy began to feel like its own project, something that could stand on its own, and needed a little longer to simmer,” said frontman Stu Mackenzie in a statement. The key differences between the two? “Alien Metal’s tracks are 143bpm and in F sharp; Entropy’s tracks are at 160bpm and in the key of A,” Mackenzie says.

entry.title: Ecco2k Sets New Album Echo
entry.summary: The follow-up to 2019’s E arrives this week
entry.content:
Seven years after releasing his debut solo album E, Ecco2k has returned with a follow-up. Echo lands on the rapper-producer’s own label, 9th, this Thursday, November 12. The record contains previously released songs “Aldehyde and Ketones” and “Sky Burial,” plus 10 additional tracks.

Per press materials, Echo follows “a vagabond character who wanders the world carrying a broadcast antenna and a crown of flowers. Moving alone through mountains and deserts, beaches, cities, and villages, he searches for signals in a world of overwhelming beauty and indifference, listening and transmitting.” Echo contains no features, and Ecco2k—real name Zak Arogundade—produced every song either solo or alongside regular collaborators Gud, Whitearmor, Felix Lee, and Mechatok.

Arogundade got his break as a musician as part of Drain Gang, the Swedish collective rounded out by Bladee, Thaiboy Digital, and Whitearmor. The crew has released two albums together thus far, 2017’s D&G and 2019’s Trash Island. Bladee and Arogundade also put out a joint album, Crest, in 2022.

entry.title: Pitchfork to Host Pavement for New Zine Launch Event

entry.content:
Pitchfork and Rough Trade are announcing a live event to celebrate the release of Pitchfork’s new zine, starring Pavement. It takes place on Wednesday, November 18, at Rough Trade Below, which is on the concourse level of 30 Rockefeller Center, in New York. Doors open at 6 p.m. Eastern Daylight Time.

Pitchfork’s new zine complements Grayson Haver Currin’s new cover story on Pavement. The event will feature Currin in conversation with Stephen Malkmus and Mark Ibold. The artist Steve Keene, known for his work with Pavement and other seminal indie rock groups, will be on-site painting attendees’ zines.

Attendees must purchase a ticket to the event in order to attend. Tickets include a free copy of the Pavement zine. Once inside Rough Trade Below, attendees can buy up to two zines at the event while supplies last. You can buy tickets at the link below.

entry.title: Palehound Announces New Album You Sing Like You’re Joking
entry.summary: Water From Your Eyes’ Rachel Brown directed the music video for lead single “Natural Disasters”
entry.content:
New York-via-Boston indie rocker Palehound is gearing up to release their first new album in nearly four years; You Sing Like You’re Joking is out February 5 via Polyvinyl. The album was co-produced with Katie Von Schleicher and Ava Luna’s Julian Fader, and features contributions from Nick Hakim. The lead single, “Natural Disasters,” gets a music video directed by Water From Your Eyes’ Rachel Brown that’s filled with gas masks, abandoned houses, and best friends holding hands. Watch it below.

“I’ve been a huge fan of Palehound since the first record, so when El asked me to collaborate on a video, I was so honored,” said Brown in a statement. “My main focus was to capture the idea of friendship and love as a memory. I think it’s necessary to hold onto the joy you felt with someone, even if they are no longer in your present life, which I think the song paints so beautifully. I also wanted to present the concept of impending societal doom as something subtle and lonely. The gas mask was a direct reference to the nuclear war imagery of the 1960s. We planned the shoot before the forecast started talking about the nor’easter, but I figured that the weather was on theme, so we continued to shoot even with governmental warnings. Strangely enough, the weather was perfectly fine pretty much all day.”

You Sing Like You’re Joking is El Kempner’s fifth full-length LP under the Palehound alias. Their last album, Eye on the Bat, came out in 2023.

entry.title: Dirty Projectors Plot 2027 Tour, Drop New Song
entry.summary: David Longstreth will perform solo sets across North America and Europe
entry.content:
Dirty Projectors are making moves ahead of the new year. For starters, David Longstreth’s band have signed to Joyful Noise; launched their own imprint, Well-Tempered Zealot; and are sharing a new single, “Jumbotron.” What’s more, Longstreth has planned an extensive solo trek in 2027, beginning in North America next spring before heading to Europe later in the summer. Check out the new song and the full list of tour dates below.

Describing the backstory of “Jumbotron,” Longstreth said,“I was thinking about the big screen and the small screen. The big tent and the kind of tent you can make in the living room with a couple couch cushions and a blanket or two. Life and entertainment; attention and volume; focus and detail; quality and value. Listen to the song!”

The most recent group effort from Dirty Projectors was their five-EP run in 2020, including Flight Tower EP. Since then, Longstreth was commissioned to write Song of the Earth, a major piece for a large ensemble, which came out digitally last year. The band’s last full-length album was 2018’s Lamp Lit Prose.

entry.title: Black Belt Eagle Scout Shares New Song “Fantasy”
entry.summary: The Swinomish musician enlisted her family members to join her in its music video
entry.content:
Black Belt Eagle Scout has returned with “Fantasy,” her first new song in three years. In that time, the Swinomish musician Katherine “KP” Paul was diagnosed with multiple sclerosis, struggled to walk, and lost the ability to play guitar. “Fantasy” delves into the stresses and struggles of a capitalistic society, and how it took a toll on her body. The single also comes with a music video directed by her cousin Priscilla Hensley and Evan Benally Atwood that features Paul’s mother, aunt, and relatives as dancers wearing handmade Iñupiat garments. You can watch it below.

“I wrote ‘Fantasy’ during a time in my life when I was transitioning out of the nonprofit world and into making music full time,” explains Paul. “I was feeling really burnt out and disconnected from the work I was doing. Working in the Native nonprofit world, I often felt this pressure to be some kind of superwoman representing Native people, while also trying to fit into systems that didn't always reflect who we are as Native people. I was at a point where I didn't want to keep trying to fit into something that didn't feel right for me anymore. I wanted to make music, feel free, spend time in the trees, and reconnect with myself outside of all those expectations.”

Black Belt Eagle Scout released her latest LP, The Land, the Water, the Sky, in early 2023, and toured heavily in support of it before she abruptly had to stop performing due to her health issues.

Revisit the Rising interview Black Belt Eagle Scout Is Bringing Queer Indigenous Stories to Indie Rock.
